note: Peer reviewed architecture taxonomy covering training pipelines, datasets and deployment issues in one place.
title: A Review on Large Language Models: Architectures, Applications, Taxonomies, Open Issues and Challenges
authors: Mohaimenul Azam Khan Raiaan et al.

reading.body:
This peer-reviewed review covers training pipelines, datasets, and deployment issues for language models in a single taxonomy.

Its value is organizational rather than novel, with 801 citations, it functions as a reference structure other researchers cite when they need a shared vocabulary for architecture types, training stages, or deployment concerns, similar to the role the more general survey by Zhao et al. plays elsewhere in this collection but focused specifically on architecture.

As a review, it does not report new experimental results, and its taxonomy reflects the state of the field as of 2024, before some of the reasoning and diffusion-model findings covered elsewhere here.

explain_beginner: Large Language Models are powerful AI systems that understand and generate human language for tasks like translation, answering questions, and creating text. This paper surveys the entire landscape of these models, explaining how they work, where they came from, and what they do well. It covers their basic building blocks, real-world uses in medicine and education, and the practical problems researchers still need to solve before these systems can be reliably deployed everywhere.
explain_business: This reference consolidates fragmented LLM knowledge into a single structured overview, enabling organizations to understand model capabilities, training requirements, and real-world deployment constraints. It clarifies practical applications across healthcare, education, and business domains while documenting unresolved challenges that affect implementation timelines and risk profiles. This informs strategic decisions about LLM adoption, resource allocation, and whether specific use cases are currently feasible or require further technological maturation.
explain_practitioner: This comprehensive review synthesizes LLM development across multiple dimensions: historical evolution, transformer architecture specifics, training methodologies, datasets, and deployment frameworks. The paper systematically catalogs existing works while documenting the complete training pipeline for LLMs. It organizes applications across diverse domains including healthcare and agriculture, then systematically identifies open technical and practical challenges that arise when implementing these models in production environments.
